challengeTypes: identify: Which of these is a computer? (Desktop vs Chair vs Table)
identify: Does a computer need electricity to work? (Yes vs No vs Only sometimes)
identify: Which is the BRAIN of the computer? (CPU vs Monitor vs Keyboard)
sort: Drag computer parts to the right category (Input: keyboard, mouse | Output: monitor, speakers | Brain: CPU)
identify: Which is NOT a type of computer? (Desktop vs Laptop vs Television)
identify: What do we use a computer for in school? (Learning vs Cooking vs Sleeping)
sort: Drag devices to computer vs not computer (Computer: desktop, laptop, tablet, smartphone | Not computer: chair, book, pencil, ball)
sort: Drag parts to input or output (Input: keyboard, mouse, microphone | Output: monitor, speaker, printer)
extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: Do NOT use speechManager.speak() anywhere in the game. Only use audioManager.play() for sound effects. Valid sound effects: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint. The game must teach: (1) A computer is a smart machine made by humans — not living, needs electricity, works fast, stores things, never gets tired. (2) Types — desktop, laptop, tablet, smartphone. (3) Uses — learning, drawing, playing games, watching videos, listening to music. (4) Parts — monitor (screen), CPU (brain), keyboard, mouse, speakers. (5) Input vs Output — keyboard/mouse send input, monitor/speakers show output. Misconceptions: 'computer is a living thing' (it's a machine, doesn't eat or grow), 'computer is a toy' (it's a smart machine, use gently), 'monitor is the computer' (monitor is only the screen, CPU is the brain). Default width=720, height=560. Use named export (export function ComputerBasicsGame), NOT export default. Export interface ComputerBasicsGameProps with width?, height?, onComplete?: (score: number) => void.
